title: How Ocarina of Time's lock-on button works
description: Ocarina of Time's Z-targeting solved a big problem in 3D combat. Here is what it does, and why the fairy is there.

scenes.say: Ocarina of Time launched in Japan on November twenty first, 1998, and its lock-on button is one of gaming's most famous controls, which we'll explain in under a minute.
Press Z, and the camera follows your target while Link keeps facing it. Arrows and other projectiles even aim at it for you.

scenes.caption: The Z trigger
scenes.say: That lets you circle around an enemy without losing sight of it, which was tricky to do in early three D games, where camera control was a real puzzle.
The design team first used a plain marker. Yoshiaki Koizumi changed it into a fairy to feel less robotic, and Navi was born.
The original scored ninety nine on Metacritic, and a Switch 2 remake arrived on November fifth, 2026. Follow for more game design secrets.
